plan:
- Electrical: Microcontroller (e.g., Arduino Mega, ESP32) for process control; pH, temperature, and gas composition (CH4, CO2) sensors; peristaltic pumps for nutrient/algae circulation; heating/cooling elements; gas flow sensor; gas storage level sensor; power supply and relays.
- Mechanical/Structural: Transparent bioreactor vessel(s) (e.g., acrylic, glass) for algae growth; mixing/aeration system (air pump, diffusers); gas collection manifold; gas storage tank (approx. 100L capacity); nutrient reservoir; plumbing (tubing, valves, connectors, check valves); support frame.
- 3D-printed parts: Custom mounts for pH/temperature probes; bioreactor lid with sealed ports for sensors, gas collection, and liquid transfer; specialized gas manifold connectors; pump enclosures; fittings for plumbing integration.
- Key processes: Algae cultivation in bioreactor, nutrient delivery, CO2 introduction, gas collection (biogas), simple gas purification (e.g., H2S removal).
- Safety: Pressure relief valves for gas storage; gas leak detection (methane sensor); proper ventilation; flame arrestors for gas lines.
- Maintenance considerations: Easy access for cleaning bioreactor, nutrient replenishment, algae harvesting, and system calibration.

subSteps.title: 3D print bioreactor lid, sensor mounts, and gas manifold connector

steps: Print the Bioreactor Lid (Main) using PETG with 30% infill, 0.2mm layer height, ensuring watertightness.
Print the pH Sensor Mount and Temperature Sensor Mount using PETG with 20% infill and 0.2mm layer height.
Print two Gas Manifold Connectors using PETG with 40% infill and 0.2mm layer height.
Print the Gas Storage Level Sensor Mount and Bioreactor Heating Element Mount using PETG with 30% infill, 0.2mm layer height, and 4 perimeters.
Inspect all printed parts for dimensional accuracy, layer adhesion, and any printing defects.
detail.summary: 3D print the bioreactor lid and all sensor/actuator mounts.

subSteps.title: 3D print pump enclosures and main controller housing
3D print sensor housings and mounts for gas system components
3D print mounts for power distribution components
Prepare power supply wiring and connect to DC-DC converter and relay module
Wire 5V power from DC-DC converter to all sensors and the main controller
Connect main controller data pins to sensors
Wire main controller GPIOs to 4-channel relay module inputs
Connect 12V power through relay module to pumps, heating element, and cooling fan
Organize and secure all wiring with cable ties
Verify all power connections and voltage outputs with a multimeter
Flash initial firmware to the main controller and verify basic functionality
Test individual sensor readings and calibrate if necessary
Test relay control of actuators (pumps, heating element, fan)
Verify serial communication with CO2 sensor
Assemble the main frame using aluminum profiles and M5 hardware
Mount the bioreactor vessel, nutrient reservoir, gas storage tank, and water scrubber vessel to the frame
Install 3D printed mounts and house electrical components on the frame
Attach sensor mounts, heating element mount, and gas manifold to the bioreactor lid and vessel
Mount the air pump and gas level sensor to the frame and gas storage tank
Connect all tubing for liquid and gas pathways, ensuring secure fittings with check valves and relief valve
Perform final cable routing, strain relief, and enclosure closing

projectDescription: This Algae Biogas Reactor is a personal system designed to produce 100 liters of natural gas weekly from algae. It features a controlled bioreactor with pH, temperature, and gas sensors, integrated pumps for nutrient delivery, and a gas collection manifold feeding into a storage tank, all managed by a microcontroller.
